stemBlocks.value: A right-angled triangle has base (x − 1) cm and perpendicular height (x + 2) cm, with an area of 30 cm². Calculate the value(s) of x and hence the lengths of the base and the perpendicular height.
Think first: Use area = ½ × base × height, and clear the half straight away by doubling both sides.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p107-q18 from workbook page 107.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the area formula using the two perpendicular sides from the diagram.
Multiply both sides by 2 to remove the fraction.
Expand and rearrange into standard form.
Apply the quadratic formula with a = 1, b = 1, c = −62.
Evaluate, reject the negative root, and find the two lengths.

contentBlocks.value: x ≈ 7.39 or x ≈ −8.39; the latter makes both sides negative. Base = x − 1 ≈ 6.39, height = x + 2 ≈ 9.39
Result: x ≈ 7.39, base ≈ 6.39 cm, height ≈ 9.39 cm

strategyBlocks.value: Write ½(x − 1)(x + 2) = 30, double both sides, expand and rearrange, solve with the formula, then reject the root giving negative lengths.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: x = (−1 + √249)/2 ≈ 7.39; base ≈ 6.39 cm and perpendicular height ≈ 9.39 cm (2 d.p.). The root x ≈ −8.39 is rejected as it gives negative lengths.

whyThisWorks.value: In a right-angled triangle the two legs are perpendicular, so they serve directly as base and height in the area formula — no extra construction is needed. Doubling first avoids carrying a fraction through the expansion. As a check, ½ × 6.39 × 9.39 ≈ 30, which recovers the given area.

commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Forgetting the ½ and solving (x − 1)(x + 2) = 30.

commonErrors.misconception: Using the hypotenuse as the height.
